verses.text: The LORD said to Moses,
"Someone may sin and be unfaithful to the LORD by cheating his neighbour. He may lie about something left in his care, or about a deal, or he may steal from his neighbour or treat him unfairly,
or he may find something that was lost and lie about it, swearing a false promise. These are some of the ways people sin.
If he has sinned in this way and is guilty, he must give back what he stole, or what he took unfairly, or what was left in his care, or the lost thing he found,
or anything he lied about with a promise. He must pay it back in full and add one fifth more. He must give it to the owner on the day he is found guilty.
Then he must bring the priest his guilt offering to the LORD: a ram from the flock with nothing wrong with it, of the set value.
The priest will make him right with God in front of the LORD, and he will be forgiven for whatever he did that made him guilty."
The LORD said to Moses,

"Give Aaron and his sons this command. This is the teaching about the burnt offering: The burnt offering must stay on the fire on the altar all night until morning, and the altar fire must be kept burning.
The priest will put on his linen robe, with linen underwear on his body. He will take up the ashes of the burnt offering that the fire has burned on the altar, and put them beside the altar.
Then he will take off these clothes, put on other clothes, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.

The fire on the altar must be kept burning. It must not go out. Every morning the priest will put more wood on it. He will lay the burnt offering neatly on it and burn the fat of the peace offerings on it.
The fire must burn on the altar all the time. It must never go out.
This is the teaching about the grain offering: Aaron's sons will offer it to the LORD in front of the altar.
The priest will take a handful of the fine flour and oil of the grain offering, with all the incense on it, and burn it on the altar as the part that is remembered, a smell that pleases the LORD.
Aaron and his sons will eat the rest of it. It must be eaten without yeast in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
It must not be baked with yeast. I have given it to them as their share of my gifts made by fire. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
Any male among Aaron's family may eat it. It is their share forever, for all their families to come, from the gifts made by fire to the LORD. Whatever touches these offerings will become holy."
The LORD said to Moses,

"This is the offering that Aaron and his sons must bring to the LORD on the day each high priest is anointed: about one and a half kilograms of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half in the morning and half in the evening.
It must be made with oil on a flat pan. Bring it well mixed with oil, and offer the grain offering in broken pieces, as a smell that pleases the LORD.
The son who is anointed priest after Aaron will offer it. It is a rule forever: it must be burned completely for the LORD.
Every grain offering of a priest must be burned completely. It must not be eaten."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell Aaron and his sons: This is the teaching about the sin offering: The sin offering must be killed in front of the LORD, in the same place where the burnt offering is killed. It is most holy.
The priest who offers it for sin will eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
Whatever touches its meat will become holy. If any of its blood is splashed on a piece of clothing, you must wash it in a holy place.
The clay pot it is cooked in must be broken. If it is cooked in a bronze pot, the pot must be scrubbed and rinsed with water.
Any male among the priests may eat it. It is most holy.
But if any of the blood of a sin offering is brought into the Tent of Meeting to make people right with God in the Holy Place, that offering must not be eaten. It must be burned in the fire.
